title: Basis-Independent Coherence Dynamics of Tripartite States under Pure Dephasing
abstract: Quantum coherence is a fundamental quantum resource whose preservation under environmental interactions is essential for quantum information processing. While most studies have focused on basis-dependent coherence measures, the dynamics of intrinsic coherence quantified by basis-independent measures remain largely unexplored. In this work, we investigate the dynamics of basis-independent quantum coherence for several representative tripartite pure and mixed states subjected to local and common dephasing environments in both Markovian and non-Markovian regimes. We show that Markovian local dephasing leads to state-dependent coherence degradation, whereas collective dephasing significantly enhances coherence preservation through decoherence-free sectors. More importantly, non-Markovian environments give rise to nearly frozen coherence dynamics for both pure and mixed states, demonstrating the remarkable robustness of intrinsic coherence against dephasing environment. A comparison with the measure of relative entropy of coherence reveals that basis-independent coherence measure exhibits substantially greater resilience and qualitatively different dynamical behaviour than its basis-dependent counterpart. These results provide new insights into the preservation of intrinsic multipartite coherence in open quantum systems and highlight basis-independent coherence as a robust quantum resource for realistic noisy quantum technologies.
summary: This paper explores how basis-independent coherence survives environmental decoherence in three-qubit systems under pure dephasing. It finds that non-Markovian effects provide superior protection compared to Markovian ones, and collective coupling enhances robustness by utilizing decoherence-free subspaces. The findings establish basis-independent measures as a more reliable indicator of intrinsic quantum resource preservation.
main_problem: The study investigates how basis-independent quantum coherence dynamics evolve for tripartite states when subjected to pure dephasing environments.
main_result: Non-Markovian environments show remarkable robustness, leading to nearly frozen intrinsic coherence, while collective dephasing enhances preservation compared to local dephasing.
method: The analysis uses the basis-independent quantum coherence measure (based on Jensen-Shannon divergence) applied to master equations describing open quantum system evolution.
model_or_system: The model considers tripartite pure and mixed states subjected to two types of pure dephasing: local (uncorrelated environmental fluctuations) or common/collective (correlated environmental fluctuations).
important_parameters: Markovian vs. non-Markovian regimes; Local vs. Common dephasing coupling strengths ($\gamma_i(t)$ and $\alpha(t)$).
main_assumptions: The analysis is restricted to pure dephasing environments, though the framework can be extended to other noise models.
figures_summary: Figures schematically illustrate local vs. common dephasing mechanisms; subsequent figures show coherence decay dynamics for mixed states under various environmental regimes (Markovian/non-Markovian).
paper_structure: The paper systematically compares basis-independent versus basis-dependent coherence measures, analyzing the time evolution of specific tripartite states ($|GHZangle$, $|Wangle$, etc.) across local and common dephasing channels in both Markovian and non-Markovian limits.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the robustness of intrinsic quantum resources (coherence) against realistic noise models, which is central to designing fault-tolerant quantum technologies.

figures.caption: Figure 1: Schematic representation of the two dephasing models considered in the present work. (a) Local dephasing model: the three non-interacting qubits A, B, and C are independently coupled to their respective bosonic reservoirs LE1, LE2, and LE3. The environmental fluctuations are therefore uncorrelated. (b) Common dephasing model: three qubits are collectively coupled to a single bosonic reservoir CE, giving rise to correlated environmental fluctuations and possible decoherence-free behaviour. These models form the basis for investigating the dynamics of basis-independent quantum coherence under Markovian and non-Markovian environments.

Figure 2: The figure shows the temporal evolution of the basis-independent coherence CBI(ρ(t)) for the four tripartite pure states, namely the |GHZ⟩, |W⟩, |WW⟩, and |Star⟩states under local and common dephasing environments in both Markovian and non-Markovian regimes.

Fig. 2(a) depicts the Markovian local dephasing model. All the four pure states show the same amount of intrinsic coherence initially, nearly 0.85.
